summary: Aluminum oxide films grown on silicon substrates by the ML-ALE method were studied. The structures were grown from trimethyl aluminum (TMA), H2O, and NO3 at temperatures in the range of 150 to 310°C. These films were characterized by refractive index n = 1.68 + 0.02 (λ = 632.8 nm) and relative permittivity ε = 5.3 + 0.2 (f = 1 MHz). The threshold voltage of the MIS structure with Al gate was about 7.5 MV/cm. The Si-Al2O3 structures had both electron and hole traps. It was found that increasing the synthesis temperature leads to a decrease of the concentration of electron traps and to an increase of hole traps. The ML-ALE method made it possible to grow Si-Al2O3 structures similar to the well-known Si-SiN structures. Si-Al2O3 structures may be used in electronic devices.
